summary: The model now follows the versioned delta path of b53551176 (the host's numbered list, deltas in flight, a receiver that misses one and reads again, a read racing a newer change, delete/move/rename forcing a fresh read, a link drop). It found 1 bug, fixed (F4: SessionListShare.set() cleared a request's stale(), so the ask after a delete could be answered from a copy that still listed the session); every window converges to the host's list, a deleted session stays out of every copy and no copy applies a change against another version within 1-2 devices, 1 hosted tab (1 window tab in MC.cfg), 2 sessions, 2 index changes, 1 link drop, an in-order link, any order on the window's two IPC paths (2.3M, 6.2M, 4.4M and 15.4M states); 18 of 18 guard mutations are DETECTED and 3 are declared equivalent. Two observations are not fixed (F5: a link that reordered would break HostSessionList; F6: the window's optimistic delete can flicker). UPDATE 30 Oct 2026 (F7): a read's answer older than the held host version replaced the copy when a change of that version applied in the same link drain (fixed in 27e13acb9; the model splits the reply into arrival and continuation, mutation hsl-keeps-older-answer). The fast tier (MC_delta.cfg 9.29M states, MC_gap.cfg, 10 sanity runs) passes; MC_two.cfg (27.3M) and MC_deep.cfg (22.6M) passed in full; MC.cfg did not finish (18.6M+ states, no violation, no verdict); 20 of 22 mutations were not rerun and the sync commit was not moved (SCOPE.md).

modeled: the host's shared numbered list (#deviceList: changed/stale/current/publish), sessions.list, sessionsChanged and its debounce, listingChanged and the snapshot, the delta or bare event to each device
the index's changes as the host sees them: create, write, rename, delete, move
the paired computer's copy of the host's list (HostSessionList: hostChanged, #read, stale), the link state and hostSessionsStale
the window tabs' register/unregister/notify and the closed-child record
the window's feed: refresh, the onSessionsChanged handler, the answer, retries, deleteSession, renameSession, reconcile/sameRow
abstracted: rows are [journal state, heldOnHost, openedBySession]; the host's read samples them in one block
the link is in order; the two IPC paths to a window have no order between them (a reply anywhere, events in order)
version numbers are integers (no epoch), generation counters are a stale flag and a clean or dirty read
a second paired device whose answers go elsewhere is a read that publishes (ForeignRead)
out_of_scope: a host that restarts, devices older than this build, retain/release of the feed, read errors' backoff, the snapshot cache
the window's optimistic hide of its own delete (F6)
other row fields, the per-device filter of SESSIONS_CHANGED, several windows of one device
assumptions: A1: the host's messages reach a computer in order (one counted encrypted socket); with a reordering link HostSessionList fails (F5)
A2: a window gets events in order and a reply at any position
A3: the host's read samples rows and tabs in one block, and every sessions.list reads again
A4: one window feed per computer and host; its read under way is its one ask (OneAsk)
A6: a host emit does not fail
A7: a handler's mutation and its listingChanged() call run in one synchronous block

findings.title: A read's answer older than the host version the copy holds replaced the copy: a change delivered in the same drain as the answer applied first and the deleted session came back
findings.story: A paired computer holds the host's list at h.1 and its copy is marked stale (a delete made through the host: hostSessionsStale). A window asks, HostSessionList#read sends sessions.list and awaits the host. The host answers at h.1 and publishes h.2 (the delete) right behind the answer. The link's #drain (wire.ts) delivers both frames in one synchronous loop: client.ts resolves the read's promise for the answer, then hostChanged(h.1 -> h.2) runs, finds held && hostVersion === base and applies it, so the copy loses the session and hostVersion is h.2. Only then does the promise's continuation run: #read sets hostVersion back to h.1 and returns h.1's rows, which the share publishes over h.2's. #announced is null (the change was applied, not announced), so nothing reads again, and the deleted session is listed again until the next change. F5 had put this down to a link that reorders and found it unreachable today: wrong, an ordered link does it.

reproduction.test: src/main/remote/host-session-list.test.ts::HostSessionList > keeps a change that applied right behind the answer of a read under way, though the answer is older (the second case, 'takes an answer that names the version a change just brought, and one newer than it', pins the neighbours)

fix.summary: HostSessionList#read compares the answer's version with the host version the copy holds (olderSessionListVersion, the one version rule in src/shared/session-list-delta.ts) and returns the copy when the answer is behind it; an answer at the same or a later version, an unnumbered one and one of another epoch still replace it. The window's feed (session-list.ts) already notes a change that arrives while its read is in flight instead of applying it, so it has no such window (a same-turn case is pinned and passes on the unchanged code); SessionListShare holds no host versions, so the guard belongs in #read. Model: the reply is split into HostReplyArrive and HostReplyResume with only the drain's HostEvents between them; the mutation hsl-keeps-older-answer removes the guard.

findings.title: A request's stale() was forgotten when another change applied: the window's next ask showed what the request had just removed
findings.story: A device deletes session s1 through its host. The host deletes the file and answers; main on the device's computer then marks its copy of the host's list stale (hostSessionsStale), because the host will publish the removal only after its 300 ms debounce. Before the window's own refresh() asks, a turn on the host writes to s2: the host publishes that change, and it applies to the version the computer's copy holds. SessionListShare.set() marked the copy current at the share's latest generation, so the stale() was gone. The window then asks and is answered from the copy, which still lists s1: the deleted session (or the old title of a rename, the old path of a move) is on screen again until the host's own change arrives. The window has just hidden the row itself, so it flashes back.

reproduction.test: src/main/remote/host-session-list.test.ts::HostSessionList > still reads the host for the ask after a request through it, when another change of the version it holds applies first; src/main/session-list-share.test.ts::SessionListShare > keeps a list stale that a list read elsewhere is applied to, so the next ask still reads

fix.summary: SessionListShare.set() publishes at the copy's own generation (this.#copyGeneration), not the latest one: an applied change is no fresher than the copy it replaces, so a stale() still waits for its read. A copy that is current stays current (its generation equals the latest one). One line and its doc comment in src/main/session-list-share.ts.

findings.title: A device keeps listing a session as held by a host tab after the tab is gone
findings.story: A window on the host holds session s1; the host re-announces a change only when #listing() differs from #listingSnapshot, which every sessions.list from any device overwrites. Device d2 lists the sessions (it sees s1 held). The window's omp reports another sessionId: sidecar-pool.ts's sessionInfoUpdate handler unregisters the file (entry.sessionFile = undefined) and calls no listingChanged(), so windowSessionFiles() no longer holds s1 but nothing was announced. Device d1 reads the list in that gap: the rows say s1 is not held and the host records that listing as its snapshot. The tab then closes: #releaseEntry notifies, listingChanged() finds the listing equal to d1's snapshot and sends nothing. Device d2 keeps the row as held on the host until something else makes it read again (a journal change, a reconnect). The same device with its two feeds (local and global scope) is enough: the snapshot is shared by every read.

changed.inFlight: (d1 :> TRUE @@ d2 :> TRUE) -> (d1 :> FALSE @@ d2 :> TRUE)
(d1 :> FALSE @@ d2 :> TRUE) -> (d1 :> FALSE @@ d2 :> FALSE)

reproduction.test: src/main/remote/host-services.test.ts::LocalHostServices > a device that listed a session as held hears of it when a window's tab lets go of it, even when another device reads the list before the tab closes (with 'control for F3'); src/main/sidecar-pool.test.ts::SidecarPool session ownership (F-OWN) > announces every take and let-go of a session file, a sessionId change's let-go too, and never a repeat

fix.summary: SidecarPool calls onSessionFilesChanged on every actual take and let-go of a session file (#registerSessionFile, #unregisterSessionFile: acquire, the `session` identity, noteSessionFile, the sessionInfoUpdate id change, release), and index.ts wires it to hostServices.listingChanged(). With every change announced when it happens, the one shared snapshot always equals the listing at the last announce or read, so no device's view stays stale (CORRESPONDENCE.md A7); a per-connection snapshot was not needed. listingChanged stays off the per-event path: a repeated get_state report changes nothing and calls nothing. Model: IdChangeAnnounces is gone, IdChange always announces; the bug is the mutation id-change-silent.

findings.title: HostSessionList let an older read overwrite a newer change: the reordering link was one way, the link's own drain is another (see F7)
findings.story: HostSessionList applies a change of the held version even while its own read of the host is under way (hostChanged checks the version before it checks the read). If the read's answer was taken before that change and arrives after it, #read sets the host version back and the share publishes the older rows over the newer ones; nothing names a later version (the change was applied, not announced), so no read follows and a deleted session is listed again until the next change. The link cannot do this today: it is one encrypted socket whose frames carry a counter and are refused out of order (wire.ts), and the host sends a reply in the continuation of the call that took it, so a reply is never older than a change that reached the computer before it. The model run with a link that lets a later event pass a reply (MC_gap.cfg) shows the result. Not reproduced in the code, because the code cannot reorder; kept as a finding of the model so a change that reorders (a second connection, a relay) meets it. CORRECTION (30 Oct 2026, F7): this finding held that only a reordering link could put a change between a read's answer and its continuation. The in-order link can too, because one drain delivers several frames before any promise continues. The guard on the answer's version that closed F7 closes this as well, and MC_gap.cfg now passes.

reproduction.test: none: the in-order link makes the interleaving unreachable

fix.summary: None applied. A guard on the answer's version in HostSessionList.#read (drop an answer older than the host version the copy holds) would close it.

findings.title: A window's own delete can be shown again for one read by an answer that was already on its way
findings.story: The window's deleteSession hides the row in the rows it shows and reads again. An answer that main computed before the delete (it is in flight on the invoke reply path, which has no order against the SESSIONS_CHANGED events) lands after the hide and accepts the older rows, so the deleted row is on screen until the queued read answers. The copies never take it back (NoReappear holds on them) and the settled view is right (ListConverges holds); only the optimistic view flickers. The same race existed before the delta commit. Seen in an earlier revision of the model where NoReappear was stated on the window's view; not reproduced in the code and not fixed, so it is out of the checked properties (SCOPE.md).

fix.summary: None applied. Dropping the answers of reads that started before the delete (the generation counter the feed keeps for release) would close it.

NeverHeld, NeverOpener, NeverGone and seven branch checks (NoHslApply, NoHslGap, NoHslNote, NoFeedApply, NoFeedGap, NoFeedNote, NoFeedRaced) are violated, so each reached state and each guard branch of the two receivers exists

mutate.ts: 18 of 18 mutations DETECTED, 3 declared equivalent with a reason written from the code (id-change-silent, hsl-skips-reread-on-gap, hsl-ignores-announced-version), no property UNCOVERED (TypeOK waived); the mutations of the three guards asked for: apply on a mismatched version (hsl-, feed-applies-on-mismatched-version), skip the re-read on a gap (feed-skips-reread-on-gap, link-up-does-not-mark-stale), an older read overwriting a newer change (feed-applies-delta-during-read, feed-ignores-announced-version); F4 is the mutation delta-clears-stale
